lines: Kessler Facility Services: a proof of concept for Jahnel Group
Watch a new request move from intake to QuickBooks while every open view updates live.
open.foot: All data is synthetic. QuickBooks is simulated.

close.title: Single Source of Truth for Everyone

segments.caption: Five views are open at once: coordinator, dispatch, controller, overview and the tech's phone.
Coordinator: a new request arrives, and Claude drafts the job from it.
The draft is labelled as Claude's. The coordinator checks it against the request as it arrived.
The new draft is already counted in the overview, under Intake draft.
Coordinator: Qualify. The overview moves the job from Intake draft to Qualified.
The estimate rises to $49,000, over this client's cap.
The contract rule holds dispatch until the client's approval is on record.
Coordinator: request the client's approval, then record it with the client's reference.
Approved for dispatch. The job lands in Ready on the dispatch screen, with no reload.
Dispatch: the recommended tech, with the reasons: skill, license, distance and load.
One click assigns Tech 1. The coordinator's record and the tech's phone update at once.
Tech's phone: the job is on the list. The tech opens it.
The tech taps Arrive. Coordinator, dispatch and the overview show Onsite.
The site signs off, and the tech closes the job and sends it to billing.
Controller: the job lands in Billing review with its invoice drafted. Every view shows the change.
The drafted invoice passes its check: signed off, approved where the contract asks, within the estimate.
Controller: Approve and submit. QuickBooks (simulated) returns an invoice number.
The aging moves: one more invoice under Current. Coordinator, dispatch and the overview show Invoiced.
Overview: how long each step waits, measured from every job's own history.
The Invoiced filter finds this job among the rest.
The one record keeps its history: each step, who took it and when.
